arxiv-1808-06416.title: Uncertainty-Complementarity Balance as a General Constraint on Non-locality
arxiv-1808-06416.creator: Liang-Liang Sun, Sixia Yu, Zeng-Bing Chen
arxiv-1808-06416.description: Abstract We propose an uncertainty-complementarity balance relation and build quantitative connections among non-locality, complementarity, and uncertainty. Our balance relation, which is formulated in a theory-independent manner, states that for two measurements performed sequentially, the complementarity demonstrated in the first measurement in terms of disturbance is no greater than the uncertainty of the first measurement.

arxiv-2106-13056.title: Morita Equivalence Classes of Tame Blocks of Finite Groups
arxiv-2106-13056.creator: Norman Macgregor
arxiv-2106-13056.description: Abstract We show that several Morita equivalence classes of tame algebras do not occur as blocks of finite groups. This refines classifications by Erdmann of classes of blocks with dihedral, semidihedral, and generalised quaternion defect groups. In particular we now have a complete classification of the Morita equivalence classes of blocks of finite groups with dihedral defect groups.

arxiv-2108-06320.title: Newton, entanglement, and the graviton
arxiv-2108-06320.creator: Daniel Carney Physics Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Berkeley, CA
arxiv-2108-06320.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniel Carney Physics Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Berkeley, CA. \Abstract

Many experiments have recently been proposed to test whether non-relativistic gravitational interactions can generate entanglement. In this note, I consider the extent to which these experiments can test if the graviton exists. Assuming unitarity and Lorentz invariance of the
S
-matrix, I demonstrate that this “Newtonian entanglement” requires the existence of massless bosons, universally coupled to mass, in the Hilbert space of low-energy scattering states.

arxiv-2203-05578.description: Abstract Bars may induce morphological features, such as rings, through their resonances. Previous studies suggested that the presence of ‘dark-gaps’, or regions of a galaxy where the difference between the surface brightness along the bar major axis and along the bar minor axis are maximal, can be attributed to the location of bar corotation.

arxiv-2211-08778.title: A Combinational Multi-Kernel Decoder for Polar Codes
arxiv-2211-08778.creator: Hossein Rezaei 1∗ , Nandana Rajatheva 1 , Matti Latva-aho 1
arxiv-2211-08778.description: Abstract Polar codes have been selected as the channel coding scheme for control channel in the fifth generation (5G) communication system thanks to their capacity achieving characteristics. However, the traditional polar codes support only codes constructed by binary ( 2 × 2 2\times 2 ) kernel which limits the code lengths to powers of 2 2 .

arxiv-2310-19655.title: Universality of the quantum energy flux at the inner horizon of asymptotically de Sitter black holes
arxiv-2310-19655.creator: Peter Hintz, Christiane K.M. Klein
arxiv-2310-19655.description: Abstract Recently, it was found that the energy flux of a free scalar quantum field on a Reissner–Nordström–de Sitter spacetime has a quadratic divergence towards the inner horizon of the black hole. Moreover, the leading divergence was found to be state independent as long as the spectral gap of the wave equation on the spacetime is sufficiently large.

arxiv-2409-17876.title: Why Companies “Democratise” Artificial Intelligence: The Case of Open Source Software Donations
arxiv-2409-17876.creator: Cailean Osborne
arxiv-2409-17876.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Cailean Osborne. Companies claim to “democratise” artificial intelligence (AI) when they donate AI open source software (OSS) to non-profit foundations or release AI models, among others, but what does this term mean and why do they do it? As the impact of AI on society and the economy grows, understanding the commercial incentives behind AI democratisation efforts is crucial for ensuring these efforts serve broader interests beyond commercial agendas.

arxiv-2501-15974.title: The correlation between the α \alpha -cluster separation and the neutron S-factor in Be 12 {}^{12}\text{Be}
arxiv-2501-15974.creator: Zhilian Cai, Qing Zhao, Zaihong Yang, Masaaki Kimura, Bo Zhou, Seung-heon Shin
arxiv-2501-15974.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhilian Cai, Qing Zhao, Zaihong Yang, Masaaki Kimura, Bo Zhou, Seung-heon Shin. The reduced width amplitudes (RWA) and the spectroscopic factor (S-factor) of α \alpha -cluster and valence neutron in 12 Be are calculated by the generator coordinates method (GCM) with the cluster model. By fixing the distance between the α \alpha -clusters’ generated coordinates, we make a theoretical experiment to analyze the relationship between the α \alpha -clustering separation and the orbital occupation of the valence neutron in 12 Be.

arxiv-2505-09276.title: Privacy-Preserving Runtime Verification
arxiv-2505-09276.creator: Thomas A. Henzinger Mahyar Karimi, K. S. Thejaswini
arxiv-2505-09276.description: Abstract Runtime verification offers scalable solutions to improve the safety and reliability of systems. However, systems that require verification or monitoring by a third party to ensure compliance with a specification might contain sensitive information, causing privacy concerns when usual runtime verification approaches are used.

In article number 2309752, Yi‐Lin Zhang, Lin‐Li Lv, Bi‐Cheng Liu, and their co‐workers map the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of macrophages in AKI‐to‐CKD transition using integration spatial single‐cell data and identified a novel subset that highly linked to fibrogenesis.

pmc-11573222.title: MALTectomy and psoriasis risk in women: A prospective study in the French E3N prospective cohort
pmc-11573222.creator: Marco Conte, Agnes Fournier, Joseph A. Rothwell, Marie-Christine Boutron-Ruault, Laura Baglietto, Marco Fornili, Emilie Sbidian, Gianluca Severi, Bandana Kumari, Karthika Paul, Karthika Paul, Karthika Paul
pmc-11573222.description: Background and aimThe involvement of mucosa associated lymphoid tissues (MALT) in the development of an autoimmune response in the skin is unclear and unstudied. In this study we sought to assess the relationship between removal of MALT tissues (MALTectomy) and the risk of development of psoriasis (overall or moderate-to-severe).

pmc-11651072.title: Optimizing Postoperative Management for PKP: Combining Traditional Chinese Medicine and Modern Rehabilitation Techniques [Letter]
pmc-11651072.creator: Chen Zhou, Zhenhua Xu
pmc-11651072.description: (ADD) following PKP has garnered attention, with potential mechanisms including thermal damage, biomechanical alterations, and disrupted nutrient pathways from bone cement.3 Reported ADD incidence ranges from 34% to 52.6%, but whether it is directly caused by PKP or a continuation of natural degeneration remains uncertain.3 Key risk factors include preoperative disc degeneration, bone cement leakage, and altered biomechanical environments.

pmc-11855049.creator: 은정 신, 현정 우
pmc-11855049.description: This study analyzes the career trajectories of students from Jeonuigam in the late nineteenth centry Joseon dynasty, shedding light on its educational functions by focusing on individuals listed in the Jeonhamsaengdoan and Byeoncheonpalsean. The primary subject of this research, the Jeonhamsaengdoan, is a valuable resource for understanding the career paths of Jeonuigam students, containing enrollment information for 384 individuals.

pmc-12558774.title: Decoding the functional plasticity of milk-derived exosomes: implications for nutrition, immunity, and therapy
pmc-12558774.creator: Shahid Hussain, Sundas Ijaz, Abdul Wajid, Abdul Qadeer, Muath Suliman, Fuad M. Alzahrani, Khalid J. Alzahrani, Khalaf F. Alsharif, Chieh-Wei Chang, Chien-Chin Chen
pmc-12558774.description: Through the targeted release of immunologically active cargo, milk-derived exosomes (MDEs) are becoming increasingly important channels for maternal-neonatal communication. This study summarizes available data, showing that the bioactivity of MDEs varies and is significantly influenced by factors such as species origin and lactation stage (colostrum versus mature milk).

pmc-12602123.title: Lipid-Mediated Sequential Recruitment of Proteins Via Dual SLIPT and Dual SLIPTNVOC in Live Cells
pmc-12602123.creator: Kristina V Bayer, Richard Wombacher
pmc-12602123.description: Cellular phenomena such as signal integration and transmission are based on the correct spatiotemporal organization of biomolecules within the cell. Therefore, the targeted manipulation of such processes requires tools that can precisely induce the localizations and interactions of the key players relevant to these processes with high temporal resolution.

pmc-12610577.title: Modular Stereoselective Synthesis of Sex Pheromone of Lambdina fiscellaria lugubrosa (Hulst) and Discovery of Cross-Species Attraction in Semiothisa cinerearia (Bremer & Grey)

pmc-12610577.description: The western hemlock looper, Lambdina fiscellaria lugubrosa (Hulst) is a destructive defoliator of coniferous forests and a major cause of economic losses in forestry. A novel and efficient stereoselective synthesis of the sex pheromone of the western hemlock looper (1, 2 and 3) has been successfully achieved.

pmc-12698700.title: Self-assembly of hybrid 3D cultures by integrating living and synthetic cells
pmc-12698700.creator: Nils Piernitzki, Ning Gao, Gilles Gasparoni, Louisa M. Krauß, Julia Schulze-Hentrich, Michael Dustin, Bianca Schrul, Balázs Győrffy, Stephen Mann, Oskar Staufer
pmc-12698700.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Self-assembly is a fundamental property of living matter that drives the three-dimensional organization of cell collectives such as tissues and organs. Here, the co-assembly of synthetic and natural cells is leveraged to create hybrid living 3D cancer cultures. We screen a range of synthetic cell models for their ability to form augmented tumoroids with artificial but controllable micro-environments, and show that the balance of inter- and extracellular adhesion and synthetic cell surface tension are key material properties driving integrated co-assembly.

pmc-13462148.creator: Qiuyi Zhang, Jiesheng Su, Suni Huang, Lihong Guo, Die Dai, Meng Zhang, Shiqi Lyu, Zesong Chen, Jianhua Chang
pmc-13462148.description: BackgroundExtensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), while often initially responsive to therapy, remains a refractory disease characterized by aggressive progression and poor long-term outcomes. Current guidelines recommend continuous treatment until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, which exposes patients, particularly long-term responders, to prolonged adverse effects and financial burden.
